title: Listening Diagnostic Test 2 - Set 2 (Cam 21 Test 2: Part 1 & Part 2)

parts.title: Part 1: Stainford College Classes
parts.transcriptHtml:
00:45ANNOUNCER: Part 1. You will hear a woman phoning to find out about one-day classes held at Stainford College.
00:54ANNOUNCER: First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 5.
01:24ANNOUNCER: Now listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 5.
01:31MAN: Hello, Stainford College External Course Registration. Can I help you?
01:36WOMAN: Yeah, I'm ringing to find out about one-day classes next year. I got a leaflet about them in the post, but I lost it. And I understand some of the classes are filling up fast, so I might need to book quite soon if I want to go ahead.
01:53MAN: Sure. Can you remember which one you were considering?
01:57WOMAN: There were a few, actually. I remember there was one on how to make Vietnamese food that sounded good. I think that was on the 13th of January. It cost about £60.
02:09MAN: Yes, you're right about the date, but it's £59, actually. It's a very popular class, and, among other things, the teacher explains how Vietnamese food includes lots of different herbs. I'm afraid that all the places are taken at present, but I can put you on the waiting list, if you want.
02:31WOMAN: No, that's OK. I'm quite interested in the bread-making class. That's in March, some time, isn't it?
02:39MAN: Yeah, the 20th of March. Would you like to register for that?
02:44WOMAN: I'm not sure. How much is it?
02:47MAN: The actual cost is £48. But then there's an extra charge as well as that for the ingredients. I'm not sure how much that is. No more than £20, I think.
02:59WOMAN: So what sorts of things do they make in the class?
03:03MAN: Oh, various types of bread. I think they make white bread, and then they make sourdough. That seems to be very fashionable at present. And they learn how to make pizza, which is apparently really good.
03:17WOMAN: Well, I'd definitely be interested in that. But there were also a few other classes that sounded interesting. I think there was one on face massage. I'd love to learn how to do that.
03:29MAN: Yeah, that's on the 23rd of February, and it costs just £35 for the day. The teacher's great. The type of massage done is a traditional technique used in India, and she actually did her training there. The massage is meant to relax you and get rid of lines and wrinkles. You practice it on yourself, so you have to take a mirror to the class so you can see what you're doing.
04:03ANNOUNCER: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 6 to 10.
04:35ANNOUNCER: Now listen and answer questions 6 to 10.
04:42WOMAN: And I think there was a class in candle making?
04:46MAN: Yes, that's sometime in April, I think. Let me check. Yes, it's on the 6th. It was on the 23rd of January, but they had to change the date. It's just £52. That's a popular course too. I think one reason why people like it is because the candles are all made out of natural products. It's filling up fast, but there's still a few places left.
05:15WOMAN: Yes, one of my friends did that class. She said the candles make really good presents. In fact, she gave me one.
05:24MAN: Ah! By the way, have you heard about the class on silk painting? That's being held on the 18th of May. You learn how to create designs on silk fabric and colour them using special dyes. Apparently people can produce beautiful artworks that way, either to put on the wall as a picture or to use for something like a scarf. It's £67.50, which is really good value, I think. There's a similar class I've seen that was £110.
06:01WOMAN: That sounds interesting. Would I need to bring the silk?
06:03MAN: No, the only thing is everyone has to bring something to protect their clothing, like an apron, if you've got one, or a shirt that you don't use anymore, because the dye can really stain your clothes.
06:18WOMAN: Right. Then the last class I was considering was a bit different. That was on DIY for beginners. I'd like to learn how to do household repairs. Are there any places left on that?
06:32MAN: That's on the 24th of February. Yes, there are a few places. It's a bit more expensive. It's £125, but it's a very popular class. You learn how to use an electric drill and a saw.
06:49WOMAN: Yeah, that would be really useful. And I even need to learn how to use a hammer, because I always end up hitting my fingers.
06:57MAN: Yes, you'll do that too. And when you've learned how to use the basic tools, you do a practical job, which is fixing a shelf to a wall.

parts.title: Part 2: Melby Heritage Walk & Coal Mine Map
parts.transcriptHtml:
08:23ANNOUNCER: You will hear some recorded information for visitors to a region about history and nature walks there and about a particular visitor attraction.
08:34ANNOUNCER: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 14.
08:59ANNOUNCER: Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 14.
09:07SPEAKER: Here is some information about history and nature walks in the region. They can be completed in less than a day and also be combined with a visit to Melby, a former coal mine now open to the public.
09:22SPEAKER: The Marsden Coastal Walk is suitable for all the family, as there are no strenuous climbs. The route begins at Marsden Harbour, where there are hourly ferries to and from the beautiful Hooker Island, a great place for fishing.
09:38SPEAKER: The walk covers part of the coastal path trail. As there are clear signposts all along the way, you don't even need to take a map with you.
09:48SPEAKER: At one point, the route goes inland slightly and passes a castle built in the 1400s, near to a now vanished market town. The castle's now just a pile of stones, but it's a great place to take photos, and fascinating information boards show what it once looked like.
10:07SPEAKER: If you set off early, you can be back in time for midday.
10:11SPEAKER: The Melby Heritage Walk is a great place to take photos, especially of the night sky. At certain times of the year, people come here from far and wide. They climb to the top of the valley and take pictures of the stars.
10:27SPEAKER: In the daytime, it's completely different. As you hike through the dense woods in the valley bottom, the only things you'll hear are the sound of your own footsteps.
10:38SPEAKER: At the highest point, you can stop to take in the views and those with lots of energy can climb the tower that's situated where there was once a 17th century hunting lodge. The route continues along the tops of the hills and brings you back down to the starting point, the car park at Melby coal mine.
11:02ANNOUNCER: Before you hear the rest of the recording information, you have some time to look at questions 15 to 20.
11:37ANNOUNCER: Now listen and answer questions 15 to 20.
11:45SPEAKER: Melby coal mine has been open to the public for 20 years and has won awards for its visitor experience. Many of the buildings around the mine are still standing and have been converted into display areas.
11:59SPEAKER: Firstly, there's an exhibition showing the history of the mine with many original black and white photos. To see that, you go from the car park via a covered walkway to the main visitor centre. Go through the ticket office to an area where there are lockers to leave heavy bags in and where you can borrow raincoats. Beyond that room is the exhibition.
12:24SPEAKER: There is a small bath house where miners used to wash after their shift underground. You can see that in the building directly to the north of the engine house. The boiler has gone from there now, but there are lines of tin baths on the stone floor.
12:41SPEAKER: There's a display of early mining tools from the days before mechanisation. You can find that in a small, L-shaped building in the middle of the northern boundary of the site. It's incredible to think how miners were able to use hand implements to cut through rock.
12:59SPEAKER: The vehicle shed, where you can find wagons of different sizes, along with some of the high-tech cutting machines that were in use until the mine closed, is in the southwest corner of the site and can be accessed via a covered walkway.
13:15SPEAKER: There is a field with ponies, which are always popular with children, on the northeastern boundary of the site, not approached via a covered walkway.
13:26SPEAKER: The other building to mention is the Education Centre. This is where school groups go when they visit the mine, but it's also accessible to the public as it contains a library and small gift shop. The centre is connected to the ticket office via a short section of covered walkway.

groups.title: Questions 15–20
groups.instructions:
Label the map below.
Write the correct letter, A–I, next to Questions 15–20.

q11.text: What does the speaker highlight about the Marsden Coastal Walk?
options: A. It requires walkers to carry a topographical map.
B. It has clear signs along the entire route.
C. It involves several steep and challenging climbs.

steps: • Dấu hiệu: 'As there are clear signposts all along the way, you don't even need to take a map'

q12.text: Visitors who reach the castle along the coastal walk will find...
options: B. information boards depicting its past appearance
C. a functioning local market nearby

steps: • Dấu hiệu: 'fascinating information boards show what it once looked like'

q13.text: Why do many people visit the Melby Heritage Walk at night?
options: A. To take photographs of the night sky and stars
B. To participate in a guided evening wildlife tour
C. To experience the absolute silence of the valley

q14.text: What can energetic walkers do when they reach the highest point of the walk?
options: A. Explore the remains of a 17th-century hunting lodge
B. Climb to the top of an observation tower
C. Take a rest in an indoor visitors' shelter

steps: • Dấu hiệu: 'climb the tower that's situated where there was once a 17th century hunting lodge'
• Dấu hiệu: Từ Ticket office qua phòng có lockers -> phòng tiếp theo là F.
• Dấu hiệu: Tòa nhà ngay phía bắc (bên trên) Engine house chính là B.
• Dấu hiệu: Tòa nhà hình chữ L nhỏ ở giữa ranh giới phía bắc chính là D.
• Dấu hiệu: Góc tây nam có lối đi mái che nối vào chính là A.
• Dấu hiệu: Khu vực góc đông bắc không có lối đi mái che chính là H.
• Dấu hiệu: Từ Ticket office có lối đi mái che ngắn đi thẳng lên phía bắc nối vào E.
